text.tspan: Each section below contains the complete musical gesture needed for that practice unit.
When an original slur, phrase, or technical connection crosses a section boundary, the neighboring measures are intentionally repeated so that Bach's notation remains intact.
Measures 1–3: One opening unit — arpeggio in G minor.
Practice the three measures as one continuous gesture; hear the harmony and keep the string crossings connected.
Measures 4–9: Three two-measure sequential units — arpeggio followed by a descending continuation.
Measures 9–11: A three-measure sequence; measure 9 also belongs to the preceding unit.
Practice 9–11 as one new direction, then connect 8–11 so measure 9 works in both contexts.
Measures 12–16: Five-measure circle-of-fifths sequence with implied voices.
Practice 12–13 and 14–15 as related cells; isolate the end of 16 into 17 before connecting the whole sequence.
Measures 17–24: Four two-measure ascending sequential units.
Practice 17–18, 19–20, 21–22, and 23–24; then connect the transitions 18→19, 20→21, and 22→23.
